chapter: New Orleans bands: Cheek, Parker, Morgan
title: How Morgan paid the band and kept credit
summary: Morgan splitting little takings after paying gas and tires, and being trusted on credit.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: What about, that one, see for yourself? Mm-hmm. You know when they say you can see for yourself? That's right.

That's how he would. That's how he would. That's how Isaiah Morgan would. Well, fellas, you come with the money in his hand like that. You can see for yourself. And how much money would that be? Well, sometime it'd be fifty cents.
For the whole band? No, you know, he'd split it up.

Fifty cents a piece. After he split it up. You could tell on how much. Because Ike, you know, he'd have to take his money out for his transportation, his gas. Sometime he had to borrow that money to get out of town from somebody, you know what I mean?
He got to pay it when it comes out. If he survived, you mean you played a dance, there won't be enough people there.

Yeah. Sometime we'd be on the way going and Ike had to stop and slide out somewhere where he knew and buy a tire. Tire's bad. Buy gas on credit. Went all the way back, well, he had to stop and pay the man. He'd take all that out that night, you know, sit down before he'd pay us.
Well, he was known to be honest then. Who? Ike, people trusted Ike.
Well, we went along with him, you know. I put it that way, we went along with him.
Yeah, but I mean the people that owned the federal station, he had good people.

Well, yeah, yeah, yeah. He had confidence in him, yeah. He could go just get credit anywhere on that highway, going toward Mississippi. Because they always paid. He'd pay them back, coming back he'd pay them back, right.
So you sometimes play a job like that and there would be very few people come to the dance? And you lose money on it?
